record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Resonances, metastable states, and trapped-set dynamics
record.original_question: In open quantum chaos for chaotic scattering systems with a fractal trapped set K, resonances λ_k of the meromorphically continued resolvent, and metastable states ψ_k or deformed L^2 eigenstates ψ̃_k, what is the precise connection between the high-energy distribution of resonances and metastable eigenstates on one hand and the chaotic dynamics on K on the other?

evidence.quote: a fractal trapped set K ⊂ S∗X, consisting of points remaining in the (compact) “interaction region” at all times.
each pole λ k of the continued resolvent is a resonance, associated with a metastable state ψ k, which decays with a half-time ∝ 1/ |Imλ k|.
What is the connection between the distribution of high-energy resonances and the eigenstates ψ̃ k on one side, the chaotic dynamics on the trapped set K on the other side?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a non-compact Riemannian manifold (or, more generally, the configuration space of a chaotic scattering system) and let $-\Delta$ denote its Laplacian (or a suitable semiclassical Schrödinger operator $P(h) = -h^2\Delta + V$). Assume the underlying classical Hamiltonian flow on the cotangent bundle $T^*X$ is hyperbolic on its trapped set
$$K \;=\; \{(x,\xi)\in S^*X : \text{the geodesic/Hamiltonian trajectory through }(x,\xi)\text{ remains in a fixed compact "interaction region" for all }t\in\mathbb{R}\},$$
and that $K$ is a fractal repeller carrying a natural hyperbolic dynamics with topological pressure, equilibrium measures, and (Hausdorff/box) dimension $d_K$.

The resolvent $R(\lambda)=(-\Delta-\lambda^2)^{-1}$ admits a meromorphic continuation from $\{\operatorname{Im}\lambda>0\}$ to a larger region of $\mathbb{C}$ (or, in the semiclassical setting, to a neighborhood of the real axis). Its poles $\{\lambda_k\}$ are the resonances; to each resonance is associated a metastable state $\psi_k$ (a generalized eigenfunction of $-\Delta$ with outgoing radiation condition, decaying in time with half-life proportional to $1/|\operatorname{Im}\lambda_k|$), or, after a complex deformation/black-box procedure, an honest $L^2$ eigenfunction $\tilde\psi_k$.

Establish the precise connection, in the high-energy limit $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_k\to\infty$ (equivalently $h\to 0$), between:

(a) the asymptotic distribution of the resonances $\lambda_k$ in horizontal strips $\{a\le -\operatorname{Im}\lambda\le b\}$ — including a sharp (fractal) Weyl-type counting law of the form
$$\#\{\lambda_k : \operatorname{Re}\lambda_k\in[r,r+1],\; -\operatorname{Im}\lambda_k\le C\} \asymp r^{d_K/2}\quad (\text{or analogous semiclassical version}),$$
the location of resonance-free strips in terms of the topological pressure $P(-\tfrac12\log J^u)$ of the unstable Jacobian, and finer features of their distribution;

(b) the phase-space concentration and equidistribution properties of the corresponding metastable states $\psi_k$ (or deformed eigenstates $\tilde\psi_k$), e.g.\ the existence and characterization of semiclassical (defect/Wigner) measures supported on $K$ and their relation to the natural hyperbolic equilibrium measures on $K$;

and

(c) the chaotic dynamics on $K$, encoded by its dimension, topological pressure, unstable/stable foliations, and equilibrium measures.

Specifically: prove sharp two-sided fractal Weyl asymptotics for resonance counts, identify the optimal width of resonance-free strips, and classify the possible semiclassical measures associated to sequences of resonant states in terms of the dynamics on $K$.
artifact.status_search_result: The connection between high-energy resonance distributions, metastable states, and chaotic dynamics on the trapped set remains an active and largely open program in quantum chaos. The conjectured fractal Weyl law has been established as an upper bound in many settings, with matching lower bounds known only in special models (e.g., open quantum baker's maps and certain hyperbolic surfaces). Recent work (2025) has even produced counterexamples showing the standard fractal Weyl upper bound is not always sharp, indicating the precise asymptotic relation is still not understood. Phase-space localization (semiclassical measures) of resonant states is similarly only partially classified.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a fractal Weyl upper bound for a class of open quantum maps; matching lower bounds remain open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bounds of fractal Weyl type are known; sharpness is largely open.

status_evidence.title: Counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for semiclassical resonances
status_evidence.snippet: Examples are constructed where the fractal Weyl upper bound is not sharp, with far fewer resonances than predicted.
status_evidence.claim: The precise high-energy resonance distribution in terms of trapped-set dynamics is still not settled.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl laws in discrete models of chaotic scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Discrete (open quantum map) models give evidence and partial proofs for fractal Weyl behavior linked to the dimension of the trapped set.
status_evidence.claim: Connection to dynamics on K is established only in toy models.
